facts.text: On this date in 1582, October 10 simply did not exist in most of Catholic Europe. The Gregorian calendar reform skipped ten days, so the 4th was followed by the 15th overnight.
On this date in 1911, the Wuchang Uprising toppled the Qing dynasty and ended 2,000 years of imperial rule in China — triggered partly by a accidentally detonated bomb in a revolutionary hideout.
Monaco has a higher density of millionaires per capita than any country on Earth: roughly one in three residents qualifies, yet the state itself runs no income tax.
The city of Chongqing, China, is home to more people than the entire country of Canada — over 32 million in its municipality, most of them unknown to global headlines.

Indonesia is the world's largest island nation and the fourth most populous country, yet its capital is actively being relocated from sinking, flood-prone Jakarta to a brand-new city being carved from Borneo's jungle.
On this date in 1987, markets worldwide were already cracking — exactly one week before Black Monday erased 22% of the Dow in a single session, the largest one-day percentage drop in its history.
On October 10, 2008, the Dow fell so violently that circuit breakers nearly triggered — it closed down 679 points, capping a week that destroyed more wealth than the entire GDP of Germany.
The NYSE's famously loud closing bell was only introduced in 1903. Before that, a gavel ended each trading day — the same way a country auction would close a sale on livestock.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2.4 trillion valuation in 2022, making it worth more than Apple, Microsoft, and Google combined at that moment.
The entire U.S. bond market — roughly $50 trillion — trades with almost no central exchange. Most of it moves through phone calls and private dealer networks, the same basic structure as the 1950s.
On this date in 1967, the Outer Space Treaty entered into force — making it illegal for any nation to claim the Moon, a rule 109 countries still follow today.
On October 10, 1846, Neptune's moon Triton was discovered just 17 days after Neptune itself — orbiting backwards, a trait shared by no other large moon in our solar system.
Your skeleton is not static. Every 10 years, your body replaces roughly 100% of its bone tissue, rebuilding itself silently while you go about your life.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
Mantis shrimp see 16 types of color receptors compared to the human three — yet process color worse than humans do, trading discrimination for raw speed of detection.
On this day in 1935, Gershwin's Porgy and Bess premiered — and was panned as too jazzy for opera fans and too operatic for jazz fans. It took decades of revivals before the world caught up to it.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Oxford dates to 1096; Tenochtitlán wasn't founded until 1325.
On this day in 1973, Spiro Agnew became the first U.S. vice president to resign in disgrace — a dress rehearsal for the president who would follow him out the door ten months later.
The fax machine was invented in 1843, twenty-three years before the typewriter. You could transmit a document across a wire before you had a reliable way to type one.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was born around 69 BC; the pyramid was finished around 2560 BC.

Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): the look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The Yaghan people of Tierra del Fuego compressed an entire negotiation of desire into a single word.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a longing for a home you cannot return to, or one that never existed. It folds grief, nostalgia, and yearning into one syllable cluster English has never managed to replicate.
On this date in 1846, the rotary printing press was patented — giving mass language its engine. The word 'press' for media descends from the literal iron screw that squeezed ink onto paper.
Saudade (Portuguese): a melancholic love for something absent. Linguists debate whether it entered Portuguese from Latin 'solitatem' or Arabic 'wahda' — loneliness may have arrived by sea either way.

On this date in 1911, the Wuchang Uprising began, toppling imperial China. The word 'revolution' itself comes from Latin 'revolvere' — to roll back — suggesting return, not rupture, was the original idea.
On this date in 2011, Bitcoin's price closed at $2.24 — exactly one year after it had traded at $0.06. The 37x gain went almost entirely unnoticed by mainstream media.
On Oct 10, 2013, the FBI auctioned 144,000 BTC seized from Silk Road — then worth ~$28M. The coins sold to venture capitalist Tim Draper, who bought them all in a single sealed bid.
Ethereum's gas limit is not set by code — it is negotiated block-by-block between miners and validators, each able to nudge it 1/1024th up or down per block.

The Bitcoin genesis block contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — Satoshi's timestamp doubles as a permanent editorial embedded in the base layer of every full node on earth.
Solana's clock drifts from real time because its proof-of-history counter is tied to compute speed, not wall-clock seconds — the chain has run as much as 30 minutes ahead of UTC.

On this date in 1997, Garry Kasparov formally demanded IBM open Deep Blue's source code and logs, alleging the machine played moves too human to be pure search — IBM declined and retired the system weeks later.

On this date in 2010, the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge published its first benchmark results, establishing the annual competition that would, two years later, be shattered by AlexNet and reorient the entire field.

GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed around 50 petaflop/s-days — roughly the same compute budget that DeepMind used to train AlphaFold 2, the model that solved protein structure prediction.
Transformers were introduced in 2017 with 65 million parameters. Seven years later, frontier models are estimated to exceed one trillion — a 15,000x increase in a single architectural generation.

Andrej Karpathy's 2022 internal Tesla presentation revealed that Autopilot's occupancy network replaced over 220,000 lines of hand-written C++ with a single end-to-end neural network trained on video.
